options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
125255.sol: Manganese ( Mn ) is a micronutrient. Excess of it in soil can cause manganese toxicity characterized by brown spots surrounded by chlorotic veins. It occurs due to (i) reduction in uptake of iron and magnesium (ii) inhibition of binding of magnesium to specific enzymes (iii) inhibition of calcium translocation into shoot apex. Therefore excess of manganese (Mn) causes deficiency of iron (Fe), magnesium ( Mg ) and calcium ( Ca ) . Hence the toxicity symptoms of Mn are actually combined deficiency symptoms of Fe, Mg

125486.subject: Botany
125486.text: What happens to leaves under water stress?
125486.sol: Even though water is one of the reactants in the light reaction, the effect of water as a factor is more through its effect on the plant, rather than directly on photosynthesis. Water stress causes the stomata to close hence reducing the CO2 availability. Besides, water stress also makes leaves wilt, thus, reducing the surface area of the leaves and their metabolic activity as well.

125796.subject: Botany
125796.text: What occupies the center of each microsporangium when the anther is young?
125796.sol: The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains. Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by four wall layers the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum. The outer three

125844.subject: Botany
125844.text: Which part of the flower represents the female reproductive part?
125844.sol: The gynoecium represents the female reproductive part of the flower . The gynoecium may consist of a single pistil (monocarpellary) or may have more than one pistil (multicarpellary). When there are more than one, the pistils may be fused together (syncarpous) or may be free (apocarpous) Each pistil has three parts the stigma, style and ovary. The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains. The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary. Insid

126508.subject: Botany
126508.text: What happens to the velocity of the enzymatic reaction as substrate concentration increases?
126508.sol: With the increase in substrate concentration, the velocity of the enzymatic reaction rises at first. The reaction ultimately reaches a maximum velocity (Vmax) which is not exceeded by any further rise in concentration of the substrate. This is because the enzyme molecules are fewer than the substrate molecules and after saturation of these molecules, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind with the additional substrate molecules

126723.subject: Botany
126723.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Cellulose gives a blue colour when treated with iodine solution. Reason (R): Cellulose is a homopolymer consisting of only one type of monosaccharide, i.e., glucose. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
126723.sol: Assertion (A) is false because cellulose does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold iodine molecules, meaning it does not give a blue colour with iodine solution. Reason (R) is true because cellulose is indeed a homopolymer composed entirely of glucose monomers. Therefore, the Assertion is false but the Reason is true. Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

126872.subject: Botany
126872.text: Carbohydrates, the most abundant biomolecules on earth, arc produced by
options: some bacteria, algae and green plant cells
fungi, algae and green plant cells
126872.sol: Carbohydrate is the most abundant biomolecule on earth. Carbohydrate is organic compound synthesized in the chlorophyll-containing cells of some bacteria, algae and green plants, during photosynthesis. Certain photoautotrophic bacteria, e.g. Green sulphur bacteria and purple sulphur bacteria contain pigments like Chlorophyll and Bacteriochlorophyll, respectively that helps them in photosynthesis. During photosynthesis, carbon dioxide reduced into carbohydrates by water and oxygen is liberated.

126910.subject: Botany
126910.text: Assertion : Living organisms are regarded as closed systems. Reason : Energy of living organisms cannot be lost or gained from the environment.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
126910.sol: Living organisms are regarded as open systems as they can lose or gain the mass or energy from the surrounding environment. All living organisms restore their lost energy either from the sunlight or indirectly from the food material.

127677.subject: Botany
127677.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients and the process is called decomposition Reason: There are only two steps of decomposition, fragmentation and leaching
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127677.sol: Decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients and the process is called decomposition. The important steps in the process of decomposition are fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation

127750.subject: Botany
127750.text: What is the percentage of photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) in the incident solar radiation?
127750.sol: Photosynthetically active radiation or PAR constitutes about 50% of the total incident solar radiation.

128030.subject: Zoology
128030.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Frogs have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies. Reason: Summer sleep is known as hibernation and winter sleep is called aestivation.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128030.sol: Frogs have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies. This protective coloration is called mimicry. During peak summer and winter frogs take shelter in deep burrows to protect them from extreme heat and cold. This is known as Summer sleep(aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation) respectively.

128062.subject: Zoology
128062.text: Frog Limbs Characteristics A. Forelimbs 1. End in four digits B. Hind limbs 2. End in five digits C. Webbed digits 3. Present in male frogs D. Copulatory pad 4. Help in swimming
128062.sol: The forelimbs end in four digits, the hind limbs end in five digits, webbed digits help in swimming, and the copulatory pad is present in male frogs.

128638.subject: Zoology
128638.text: Catecholamine in a normal person induces
128638.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. These are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of fight or flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating, etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respirat

128661.subject: Zoology
128661.sol: The functions of hypothalamus include thermoregulation, water balance and control of hormone functions. It is located below the thalamus and is a part of limbic system. It synthesises and secretes certain neurohormones which in turn stimulate or inhibit the secretion of pituitary hormones. It controls other activities also like sleep, hunger, body temperature, etc.

129152.sol: Neutrophils are most abundant granulecytes which engulf microbes by phagocytosis. These have 2-7 lobulated nucleus and do not stain any basic or acidic dye monocytes are large sized leucocytes, which are highly motile and phagocytic in nature.

129918.subject: Zoology
129918.text: What is the function of spirometer?
options: To create pressure gradients between the atmosphere and the alveoli
To estimate air volume involved in inspiration and expiration
129918.sol: An increase in pulmonary volume decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than the atmospheric pressure which forces the air from outside to move into the lungs, i.e., inspiration Relaxation of the diaphragm and the inter-costal muscles returns the diaphragm and sternum to their normal positions and reduce the thoracic volume and thereby the pulmonary volume. 130321.subject: Zoology
130321.text: Choose the correct statement w.r.t diagram shown: Assertion: Ribs are called Bicondylar. Reason: Ribs have two articulation surfaces on its ventral end.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Both Assertion and reason are false.
130321.sol: There are 12 pairs of ribs. Each rib is a thin flat bone connected dorsally to the vertebral column and ventrally to the sternum. It has two articulation surfaces on its dorsal end and is hence called bicephalic.

130496.subject: Zoology
130496.text: Achondroplasia is a disease related with the defect in the formation of
130496.sol: Achondroplasia is a disorder inherited as dominant characteristic in which bones of arms and legs fail to grow to normal size due to defect in both cartilage and bone. It results in a type of dwarfism characterised by short limbs, a normal sized head and body and normal intelligence.

131589.subject: Zoology
131589.text: What is the role of permease in the lac operon?
options: Hydrolysis of lactose into its monomeric units
Transport of lactose into the cell
131589.sol: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene – here the term i does not refer to inducer, rather it is derived from the word inhibitor) and three structural genes (z, y, and a). The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. options: Genetic mapping of the human genome

Polymorphism (variation at genetic level) arises due to mutations. New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). 132110.subject: Zoology
132110.text: How do factors occur according to Mendel's Law of Dominance?
132110.sol: (i) Characters are controlled by discrete units called factors. (ii) Factors occur in pairs . (iii) In a dissimilar pair of factors one member of the pair dominates (dominant) the other (recessive). The law of dominance is used to explain the expression of only one of the parental characters in a monohybrid cross in the F1 and the expression of both in the F2 . It also explains the proportion of 3:1 obtained at the F2 .

Alleles disappear in the F1 generation

Though the parents contain two alleles during gamete formation, the factors or alleles of a pair segregate from each other such that a gamete receives only one of the two factors. 133053.subject: Zoology
133053.text: Which one of the following is reptilian ancestor of birds?
133053.sol: The first fossil birds found in the rocks of Jurassic period belonged to genera Archaeopteryx and Archaeornis. These are considered as reptilian ancestors of birds. It was about the size of a crow and possessed feathers and wings but had a long reptilian tail very much unlike the modern birds and a toothed beak. Fossils of Hesperornis, an aquatic diving bird, and Ichthyornis, a powerful flying bird, have been found from Cretaceous.

133151.subject: Zoology
133151.text: When is a person considered not healthy?
options: When they have a balanced diet and regular exercise
When they have good mental health
133151.sol: Good health can be maintained through a balanced diet, personal hygiene, regular exercise, awareness about diseases, proper disposal of waste, control of vectors, and hygienic food and water resources. Diseases can be broadly categorized into infectious and non-infectious diseases. Infectious diseases are easily transmitted from person to person, while non-infectious diseases include cancer and other health conditions. They infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs. The common cold is characterised by nasal congestion and discharge, sore throat, hoarseness, cough, headache, tiredness, etc., which usually last for 3-7 days. 133514.text: Retroviruses have their genetic material in the form of:
133514.sol: AIDS is caused by the Human Immuno deficiency Virus (HIV), a member of a group of viruses called retrovirus, which have an envelope enclosing the RNA genome.

134381.subject: Zoology
134381.text: Golden ages of reptiles and fishes are respectively
134381.sol: Mesozoic period was golden age for reptiles. In this period reptiles were dominant species, like dinosaurs. Devonian period was golden age for fishes due to their abundance and diversity.

134880.subject: Zoology
134880.text: A researcher is attempting to isolate pure DNA from a bacterial culture. Which of the following pairs of enzymes should be used to first break open the bacterial cells and subsequently remove the contaminating RNA from the resulting mixture?
134880.sol: To isolate DNA from bacterial cells, the bacterial cell wall must be degraded using the enzyme lysozyme. During the subsequent purification process, contaminating RNA is removed by treating the mixture with ribonuclease (RNase). Protease is used to remove proteins, not RNA. DNase is strictly avoided because it would destroy the target DNA molecule itself. Cellulase is used to break open plant cells, not bacterial cells. Answer: Lysozyme and Ribonuclease

134970.subject: Zoology
134970.text: Following statements describe the characteristics of restriction endonucleases. Identify the incorrect statement.
options: The enzyme cuts DNA molecules at identified position within the DNA.
The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands.
The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific site on each strand.
The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.
134970.sol: DNA consists of two complementary strands of nucleotides that spiral around each other in a double helix. Restriction enzymes cut through both nucleotide strands, breaking the DNA into fragments. These are the endonucleases that are used in RDT or genetic engineering techniques.

95372.sol: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical, while their larvae is bilaterally symmetrical. They are triploblastic and coelomate organisms. 97218.sol: Wheat is a long day plant. These plants flowers only when they exposed to critical photoperiod or photoperiod longer than their critical day length. These plants give flowers on exposure to photoperiod equal to or shorter than their critical day length. They need a continuous (uninterrupted) dark period for flowering.
